verses.1: And at the time when the locusts departed, David sent Joab and his men, along with all of Israel. They attacked the people of Ammon’s kingdom. Then David ruled over Jerusalem.
verses.2: And it was morning. David got up from his bed. He walked around the roof of the king’s house. He saw a woman washing herself on the roof. The woman was very beautiful to look at.
verses.3: And David sent for a woman to be brought to him. He said, “This is Sephiah, daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Chittite.”
verses.4: David sent his servants to take her away. She came to him, and he lay with her. She became holy through her virginity, and then she returned to her house.
verses.5: And the woman got up and went to tell David. She said, “Behold, I am.”
verses.6: David sent Uriah to Joab. Joab then sent Uriah to David.
verses.7: And Uriah came to him. David asked him to bless Joab, and also to bless the people and those who were fighting in battle.
verses.8: And David said to Uria, “Go into your house and wash your feet.” So Uria left the king’s house, and he followed behind him, carrying the king’s things with him.
verses.9: And Uriya entered the king’s house, along with all of his servants. But he did not go down into his own house.
verses.10: And they told David, “Urie will not come to your house.” David said to Urie, “Surely you didn’t come here knowing that you wouldn’t be able to go into your own house.”
verses.11: And Uria said to David, “The people of Israel and Judah are living in their cities. Your servants, Joab and his men, are stationed at the gates. I will go into my house to eat and drink, and to lie with my wife. May your life be blessed, my lord.” If I do what you say.
verses.12: And David said to Uriah, “Stay here today as well. Tomorrow, I will send for you.” And Uriah stayed in Jerusalem on that day and the following day.
verses.13: David called for him, and he ate before him. Then David bought him and sent him away in the evening to sleep in his bed with the servants of Adonai. But he did not go down into his house.
verses.14: In the morning, David wrote a list for Joshua. Then he sent it to Urie.
verses.15: And it was written in the record, “Bury Uria at the edge of the battlefield. Then they will return from their enemies and die.”
verses.16: And in Shmonor Yoav went to the city. He gave Uriya to the place where he knew that the people of Chayil were located.
verses.17: And the people of the city went out and fought against Yoav. Many of the people of David’s army were killed. Also, Uriyah the Hittite died.
verses.18: And Joshua sent and reported to David all the details of the battle.
verses.19: And he commanded the priest, “Just as you have spoken all these words about warfare, so also speak them to the king.”
verses.20: And if she were to bring the king’s armor with her, and say to you, “Know that you should go to the city to fight.” But they won’t know what will happen to them from above.
verses.21: Who killed Abimelech, the son of Jerubbaal? A woman threw sand on him from above the roof. He died in that place. Why did you rush towards the house? And you said, “Your servant Uri also has died.”
verses.22: And the angel went and reported to David all that Yoab had sent.
verses.23: And the angel said to David, “The people have become stronger than us. They have come against us from all sides. They will be able to reach the entrance of the gate.”
verses.24: And the priests were killed by your servants from above the furnace. They died along with the servants of the king. And your servant Uria also died.
verses.25: And David said to the prophet, “Say to Joab that he may not harm this city in your eyes. For such is its fate: it will be destroyed by your forces.”
verses.26: And Eshta Uriya heard that Uriya had died. So she mourned for her husband.
verses.27: And when the mourning period was over, David sent for her and brought her back to his house. She became his wife, and she gave birth to a son for him. But things did not go well with David, because of what David did in the eyes of Jehovah.
